author_prompt:
Author 8 DIFFERENT natural ecommerce customer-service dialogue families in en.
Batch 16; ensure at least four current turns classified as account_security across this batch.
Each family has its OWN coherent history of 2, 4 or 6 short alternating user/assistant
messages, followed by 3 ALTERNATIVE current user turns, not three sequential turns.
Those alternatives differ in effective intent: retain vs replace, withdraw vs
continue, single goal vs concurrent goal, or resolved vs unresolved reference.
Include natural short answers where history matters. Vary old completed tasks,
hesitation, self-correction, indirect wording, topics and dialogue acts. General
and human-service requests must also occur as NEW goals, not only stale history.
Do not follow a repeated sentence template or substitute product nouns to create
new families. Avoid stereotyped 'information only, do not submit' repetition.
Invent broad everyday ecommerce situations; no copied benchmark or private data.
History plus current turn should fit 150 English words or 180 Chinese characters;
keep it compact but meaningful. No future replies or final conversation summaries.
Supply the correct label for each alternative according to the rubric.

families.scenario: Customer locked out of account after changing phone number

messages.content: I changed my phone number last week and now I can't get the verification code to log in.
I'm sorry to hear that. I can help you verify your identity another way. Could you confirm the email address on the account?
It's jordan.kim@gmail.com. I still have access to that inbox.
Great, I've sent a one-time link to that email. Click it and you'll be able to set a new password and update your phone number.

variants.text: I clicked the link but it says expired. Can you resend it?
variants.label: account_security

variants.text: Actually, forget it. I'll just make a new account instead.
variants.label: __DEFER__

variants.text: Thanks for the help. Also, do you carry replacement straps for the Series 5 watch?
variants.label: product_technical

families.scenario: Customer asks about a refund for a damaged item

messages.content: The ceramic mug set I got yesterday arrived with two cracked mugs.
Oh no, I'm sorry about that. I can start a return and refund for you. Would you like a replacement or a refund to your original payment method?
A refund is fine. It was order #48291.
Perfect, I've submitted the refund request. You'll see the amount back on your card within 5-7 business days after we receive the return.

variants.text: Wait, actually I'd rather get a replacement instead. Can you switch that?
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Okay thanks. And can you tell me if my account has any saved addresses I should remove?
variants.label: account_security

variants.text: Hmm, actually I think I want to speak to a supervisor about how this was packed.
variants.label: human_service

families.scenario: Customer asks about delivery timing for a gift

messages.content: I ordered a birthday gift for my sister on Tuesday. Order #7734. It's supposed to arrive Friday but I'm nervous.
Let me check the tracking for order #7734. One moment please.
It's currently at the regional hub in her city and scheduled for delivery Friday before 8 PM. You should be all set.

variants.text: Great, thanks. Oh and I noticed a charge on my statement from you guys that I don't recognize. Can you look into it?
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Actually, I need it by Thursday now. Is there any way to expedite it?
variants.label: order_logistics

variants.text: Perfect. By the way, I think someone logged into my account from another country last night. Can you check recent logins?
variants.label: account_security

families.scenario: Customer asks about compatibility of a laptop charger

messages.content: Will the 65W USB-C charger work with my 2021 MacBook Pro 14-inch?
Yes, it's fully compatible. The 14-inch MacBook Pro supports USB-C Power Delivery up to 96W, so a 65W charger will work, though charging may be a bit slower under heavy load.
Okay, and does it come with a cable in the box?
Yes, a 1.8m USB-C to USB-C cable is included in the package.

variants.text: Alright, I'll take it. Actually, hold on—can I use my old 30W charger from my phone instead? Would that damage anything?
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Good enough. Also, I've been getting password reset emails I didn't request. Should I be worried?
variants.label: account_security

variants.text: Thanks, that's all I needed. Have a nice day.
variants.label: general

families.scenario: Customer wants to cancel an order before dispatch

messages.content: I need to cancel order #9021. I accidentally ordered two of the same desk lamp.
Let me check if it's already been dispatched. One moment.
Good news—it hasn't shipped yet. I can cancel it right away. Shall I proceed?

variants.text: Yes please cancel it. And while you're at it, can you remove my saved payment card from the account?
variants.label: account_security

variants.text: Actually, keep one of them. Just cancel the duplicate order instead.
variants.label: order_logistics

variants.text: Hmm, actually I changed my mind—I want both after all. Please don't cancel anything.
variants.label: order_logistics

families.scenario: Customer asks about warranty coverage on headphones

messages.content: My wireless headphones stopped pairing after three months. Do they have a warranty?
Yes, they come with a 12-month manufacturer warranty. I can help you file a claim. What's the order number?
Order #1187. I bought them in March.
Thanks, I've located the order. I'll email you a prepaid return label for the warranty claim.

variants.text: Actually, I don't want to deal with mailing them back. Is there a troubleshooting step I can try first?
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Before I do that—can you confirm what email address you have on file for me? I want to make sure it's the right one.
variants.label: account_security

variants.text: Never mind, I'll just buy a new pair instead. Thanks anyway.
variants.label: __DEFER__

families.scenario: Customer asks about a missing item in a delivery

messages.content: My order #3350 arrived but the coffee beans are missing. Only the grinder came.
I'm sorry about that. Let me check the packing slip for that order.
It looks like the beans were split into a second shipment that should arrive tomorrow. You should receive a tracking email shortly.

variants.text: Oh okay, that's a relief. Also, I think my account password was changed without my permission. Can you help me check?
variants.label: account_security

variants.text: I don't trust that. I want to file a complaint about this whole situation.
variants.label: human_service

variants.text: Alright, but if it doesn't come tomorrow I'm going to want a refund for just the beans.
variants.label: order_logistics

families.scenario: Customer asks about a discount code not applying

messages.content: I tried using code SAVE20 at checkout but it says invalid. The email said it was for my account.
Let me look into that code for you. Can you tell me the email address associated with your account?
It's maria.lopez@outlook.com.
I see the issue—the code was sent to a different account under maria.lopez@gmail.com. Would you like me to apply the discount manually to your current cart?

variants.text: Oh, I don't even remember having a gmail account with you. Can you tell me what orders are on it?
variants.label: account_security

variants.text: Yes, please apply it manually. I'm checking out right now.
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Actually, that gmail account is my old one. Can you merge both accounts together?
variants.label: account_security
